That may be true, but is probably just misleading. Presumably by "Christianity" you mean the Roman Catholic Church, and you are talking about the persecution of Galileo.

The reality is, both the church and the scientific community of the time were divided on the question of heliocentrism. And for most of the duration of the controversy, Galileo enjoyed the personal support of the Pope himself. Far from the mere suggestion of heliocentrism being banned, Galileo was permitted to write on it as a possibility or theory, just not claim it was The Truth. Given the state of the scientific evidence at the time, this was in some sense not just a compromise to keep Galileo out of trouble, but actually a reasonable evaluation of heliocentrism.

What finally got Galileo in the most trouble and placed under house arrest was not promoting heliocentrism per se, but writing a book that seemed to ridicule the same Pope who had always defended him.
